title: Getting Started
intro: This tool turns a one-line prompt into either a GTA5 mission script or a ready-to-open Unity project. Below are the three things you need to do once.

steps.title: 1. Wire up a chat backend
steps.body: Generation needs a local LLM. Open the Backends page and pick either LM Studio (default :1234) or Ollama (:11434). Start the server, load a model, then click Test Connection. The Chat light at the top right should turn green.

steps.title: 2. (Optional) Build the local RAG index
steps.body: Asset resolution is sharper with RAG. Run `python main.py rag-build` (gta5 corpus) and `python main.py rag-build --unity` (Unity corpus) to build the local ChromaDB index — no server or API key needed. The RAG light turns green once both domains are indexed. If you don't want RAG, flip Basic Mode on and the project uses bundled local lookup tables instead.

steps.title: 3. Generate your first mod or project
steps.body: Open the Prompt page, pick GTA or Unity at the top, type one sentence (e.g. 'Infiltrate the docks at night and steal a drug shipment'), and click Generate. Watch the live progress; the output file appears below when done. GTA mods need ScriptHookV + ScriptHookVDotNet3.dll installed — you'll get a reminder on the output panel.

steps.title: 4. Manage what you've made
steps.body: Every run is saved under output/ (GTA) or output/unity/ (Unity). The Library page lists everything with star ratings, a Share button (copies the path to clipboard), and an Open button (reveals the folder in Explorer).

tips: Custom Args on the Prompt page accepts CLI-style flags. --debug streams LLM request/response bodies into the live progress console.
The Errors & Fixes page is a searchable cheat sheet for the most common failures: backend not started, no model loaded, RAG unauthorized, truncated JSON, and more.
Saved settings persist in config.yaml. The CLI (python main.py generate ...) reads the same file, so the two stay in sync.
